page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Tau T2D machine family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. With 1.0 thread per core, this instance provides dedicated physical execution resources without simultaneous multithreading. The hardware configuration includes 16 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced ratio of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. No local storage or GPU accelerators are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core metrics placing in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench scores, and Passmark CPU evaluations consistently register in the average range. Memory bandwidth tests, including read-only and write operations on large blocks, also align with middle-tier performance profiles. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput represent relative performance bottlenecks, falling into the bottom 25% tier.

This instance offers a balanced resource profile suitable for general-purpose workloads. The dedicated AMD EPYC cores provide reliable execution for application servers, software compilation, and moderate database operations. Given the absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs, it is best suited for workloads that rely on network-attached storage and do not require hardware acceleration, such as microservices, development environments, and light-to-medium web serving.
